text: Code Memory（CM）是接入 DSH 的本地代码索引与上下文检索插件。它在 Harness 每轮开始时按用户问题检索相关源码，并通过工具提供受字节预算限制的上下文；索引可包含符号、代码单元和依赖关系，也支持本地更新。主要用途包括自动补充编码上下文、查找符号与代码、读取相关依赖，以及通过 MCP 为其他编码客户端检索项目源码。适合希望减少手动找代码步骤的开发者。插件自身不要求 API 密钥；检索到的代码会加入 Harness 对话，后续模型请求由用户配置的模型服务处理。

Code Memory (CM) adds local code indexing to DSH and retrieves bounded source context for each Harness turn. It also offers symbol and dependency lookup through tools and MCP. No plugin API key is needed; retrieved code enters the Harness conversation handled by the user's configured model service.
让 DSH 在每次回答前先找出和我问题相关的项目源码。
我不想手动翻文件，能按任务自动补充代码上下文吗？
想从代码库里搜索某个函数、类或符号，并看到它所在源码。
能不能沿着代码依赖关系展开相关定义和调用位置？
I need my coding assistant to retrieve relevant local source files for each task.
How can I query project symbols and fetch bounded source context through MCP?
Code Memory 的功能「自动补充上下文」：Harness 每轮开始时读取用户问题，用本地索引检索相关源码，并将结果作为上下文加入对话。
Code Memory 的功能「符号与依赖检索」：索引 JavaScript/TypeScript 源码中的符号和关系；按问题查找候选代码片段，并可展开相关节点与依赖。
Code Memory 的功能「MCP 源码检索」：MCP 客户端可调用 cm_retrieve_context 获取带快照标识的局部源码上下文，也可查询项目索引和向量状态。
dsh-plugin-code-memory 提供工具 cm_retrieve_context
dsh-plugin-code-memory 提供工具 cm_project_status

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Code Memory for DeepSeek Harness：**Give your coding agent the relevant source before its first step.** Code Memory (CM) is a local code index and context plugin for JavaScript and TypeScript projects. It combines symbol lookup, dependency graphs, and semantic search to reduce repeated source discovery.

**Unofficial community project.** Independently developed; not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Code Memory for DeepSeek Harness：**English** · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [Download v0.9.3](https://github.com/kobubu/Rag-Coding/releases/tag/v0.9.3) · [Windows installation](docs/INSTALL-WINDOWS.md)

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · What it does：- Supplies compact source context before the first model call in DeepSeek Harness.
- Looks up named files and symbols directly; uses local MiniLM embeddings and LanceDB when discovery is needed.
- Expands relevant dependencies using the TypeScript compiler's symbol and call graph.
- Checks source versions and avoids repeating unchanged whole files already supplied to Harness.
- Exposes an MCP server for Codex and Claude Code and an optional `UserPromptSubmit` hook for automatic context.
- Includes CM Atlas, a local map of modules, symbols, and their relationships.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · What it does：The index, embeddings, and graph stay on your computer. Selected code is still sent to your model provider when you use a cloud model. CM does not include model credits or a model-provider subscription.

Actual CM Atlas screenshot of this repository's public `src` directory: 39 modules, 2,409 symbols, and 8,321 relationships. The current Atlas interface is in Russian; the installation guide below is in English.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Measured results, with limits：The published Harness pilot used GPT-6 Luna on **six task types in one repository**, Geo Dash. Three evaluation series each ran 36 sessions: no CM, the earlier CM, and the newer CM, with two repeats per task and arm.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Measured results, with limits：| Newer CM versus no CM | Published result |
|---|---:|
| Total model tokens | 45–66% fewer across the three series |
| Estimated model price | 30–47% lower |
| Total Harness session time | 18–37% lower |
| Independently checked solutions, pooled across series | 36/36 with newer CM; 35/36 without CM |

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Measured results, with limits：These are **small, single-project pilot results**, not guaranteed savings. The ranges are observed series results, not confidence intervals. Costs are estimates; session time does not include first-time installation or indexing. All attempts, including failures, are retained. Earlier approaches and native-client experiments have different outcomes; do not transfer these percentages to every client or workload.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Codex and Claude Code：In Codex and Claude Code, CM adds its context through a `UserPromptSubmit` hook served by a warm local daemon; the installer configures it. Fourteen tasks in the same repository — the six above plus eight new ones that CM was not tuned on — three repeats per task and arm, 84 sessions per client:

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Codex and Claude Code：| CM versus no CM | Codex, GPT-6 Luna | Claude Code, Sonnet 5.5 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Independently checked solutions | 41/42 vs 40/42 | 42/42 vs 42/42 |
| Total model tokens | 58.0% fewer | 40.4% fewer |
| Estimated / reported price | 29.0% lower | 18.0% lower |
| Total session time | 35.9% lower | 35.1% lower |
| Median session | 7.3 s vs 12.2 s | 12.4 s vs 18.7 s |

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Codex and Claude Code：In both clients the paired 95% bootstrap intervals for tokens and time exclude zero. Three larger tasks — a feature across three modules, a rename across imports, a new parameter in several places — also gain: Codex 60.1% fewer tokens and 39.2% less time, Claude Code 35.0% and 16.4%. One weak spot is documented: on a rewrite of a counting function, agents with CM more often lose a key-coercion detail and need a second edit. Two unrelated public libraries that CM was not tuned on, six tasks each, confirm the effect: node-semver — Codex 59.1% fewer tokens and 49.0% less time, Claude Code 38.2% and 18.0%; superstruct (TypeScript) — Codex 39.2% and 27.4%, Claude Code 28.6% and 12.0%, with an 8.3% lower price. Three projects are still not a guarantee for other workloads. The MCP server alone, without the hook, showed no savings.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Install into an existing Harness：Requires DeepSeek Harness **0.2.0-rc.2** and Node.js 24 or 22.19+ within 22.x:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:kobubu/Rag-Coding#v0.9.3
```

The tag contains the compiled plugin, CLI entry points, and Atlas. CM needs no installation build or Vite/React runtime modules. Then [prepare the project index and local model](docs/DEEPSEEK-PLUGIN.md#github-installation). A ready release tarball is also available:

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Install into an existing Harness：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/kobubu/Rag-Coding/releases/download/v0.9.3/dsh-plugin-code-memory-0.9.3.tgz
```

Git tags before 0.9.1 require their release tarball or an explicit source build. The new runtime works with scripts disabled; native dependencies follow the host package manager's policy.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Install into an existing Harness：If CM was installed with the Windows bootstrap, update it using the new ZIP and the same `-InstallRoot`. Harness 0.2.0-rc.2 can prefer a CM copy beside its own installation over a profile-installed copy; adding another Git dependency to that older installation does not replace its launcher or embedded copy. The bootstrap creates a new release directory and switches managed project launchers.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Install on Windows：Download **CM-0.9.3-Windows.zip** and **SHA256SUMS.txt** from the [v0.9.3 release](https://github.com/kobubu/Rag-Coding/releases/tag/v0.9.3), verify the checksum, and extract the ZIP. From the extracted folder, run:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install_cm.ps1 -ProjectRoot 'C:\path\to\your-project' -Clients harness
```

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Install on Windows：The installer uses a compatible Node.js or downloads a private runtime, installs CM and Harness **0.2.0-rc.2**, downloads the embedding model, and prepares your index. Administrator rights and a source checkout are not required. Internet access is required for the initial dependencies and model downloads. Open the generated `start-harness.ps1` path printed by setup, then configure your model provider in Harness.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Install on Windows：Use `-SourceScope src` to index a subdirectory. Use `-Clients harness,codex,claude` to add project MCP connections for all three clients; Codex and Claude Code must be installed separately. Their automatic-context hook is currently a **separate manual setup**, not an installer default.

[Install, launch, verify, and remove](docs/INSTALL-WINDOWS.md) · [Native-client hook setup](docs/NATIVE-CLIENTS.md)

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Build from source：Use Node.js **24 LTS**, or Node.js **22.19.0+ within the 22.x line**.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kobubu/Rag-Coding.git
cd Rag-Coding
npm ci
npm run verify

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Build from source：`plugin:smoke` checks both legacy and compact tools, automatic context, filesystem observations, and unload through the real Harness runtime without a model call. In PowerShell, use `npm.cmd` for commands that forward flags. For restricted cloud builds, `ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL=skip npm ci` skips the native runtime download; running local embeddings still requires a working ONNX runtime.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Build from source：The Windows bootstrap is the packaged installation path. A macOS/Linux installer, automatic release updates, and a subscription service are not included.

For source changes, `npm run compile` rebuilds the runtime. Commit matching `dist/src/` and `dist/viewer/`; `npm run package:check` and CI reject missing/stale artifacts. The command is named `compile` because npm treats a script named `build` as a reason to rebuild Git dependencies.

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Documentation：CM is written in TypeScript/Node.js. Project code is indexed without being executed. Supported inputs are JavaScript/TypeScript source files; current corpus limits are 500 files and 8 MiB of source. See [contribution rules](CONTRIBUTING.md).

dsh-plugin-code-memory README · Try it on another repository：Independent A/B results are welcome: use the same task, model, reasoning settings, checks, and starting commit with CM on and off. Include indexing/setup time separately, all failed attempts, total tokens, elapsed time, and whether the patch actually passes independent checks. Report regressions as well as wins in [Issues](https://github.com/kobubu/Rag-Coding/issues).
